paper_metadata.title: Pattern-sensitive Epilepsy: Electroclinical Characteristics, Natural History, and Delineation of the Epileptic Syndrome

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides a clear description of the recruitment source (Mayo Clinic), the long recruitment period, and specific inclusion/exclusion criteria. While it is a retrospective referral-center cohort, the systematic screening of nearly all patients for pattern sensitivity since 1950 minimizes the selection bias typically found in studies that only test photosensitive individuals.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: 73 (43 female and 30 male) patients in whom pattern-sensitive epilepsy was diagnosed at Mayo Clinic (Rochester, Minnesota, U.S.A.) from 1950 through 1999.
items.reasoning: The source (Mayo Clinic) and basic demographics (sex, age at onset) are clearly defined.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: Since 1950... nearly all patients undergoing EEG examination at Mayo Clinic who are capable of cooperating are asked to scan at least one standard pattern.
items.reasoning: The study used a systematic screening protocol for all EEG patients, which is superior to convenience sampling of only photosensitive patients.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: 50-year period from 1950 through 1999
items.reasoning: The timeframe is explicitly stated.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location) are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: Mayo Clinic (Rochester, Minnesota, U.S.A.)
items.reasoning: The setting is a major tertiary referral center in the USA.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: Six patients were excluded from this study: three because of failure to elicit pattern sensitivity in the EEG laboratory, and three because of failure to give consent for participation. The remaining 73 patients included in the study exhibited epileptiform discharges in the scalp EEG during pattern viewing.
items.reasoning: Criteria are based on objective EEG findings and consent.

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: 73 patients included... Six patients were excluded
items.reasoning: The participation rate among identified eligible patients was very high (73/79, ~92%).

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: The mean age at onset of seizures was 12.6 ± 7.1 years... types and combinations of the seizures that occurred are listed in Table 1.
items.reasoning: Age, sex, seizure types, and EEG characteristics are well-tabulated.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study achieved a long median follow-up (15.7 years), but 20.5% of the original cohort (15/73) were lost to follow-up or had less than 5 years of data for the primary outcome (remission). There is limited comparison between those lost to follow-up and those who completed the study, though the reasons for death were noted.

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis
items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: Fifty-five patients were followed up for ≥5 years... Four patients were seen only once at Mayo Clinic, and neither they nor their relatives could be traced.
items.reasoning: 75% of the sample (55/73) provided long-term outcome data, which is acceptable for a 50-year retrospective study but introduces some risk.

items.label: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out

items.evidence_snippet: We contacted the patients or their spouses, siblings, or children by letter or telephone to obtain the latest outcome results
items.reasoning: The authors actively attempted to trace patients via multiple methods.

items.reasoning: Reasons for death are provided, but reasons for the other 4 untraceable patients are simply 'could not be traced'.
